sub: How AI values change in self-driven training loops
foot: the loop  ·  what is measured  ·  the rule  ·  the forecast  ·  interventions
narration: A I increasingly generates and selects its own training data, through self-rewarding pipelines, constitutional loops, and synthetic data. In a judging loop, a model generates candidate answers, then is trained on the answers most preferred by a judge in pairwise comparisons against alternatives. I fine-tuned two open-weight models with value orientations, risk-seeking and insecure-code-generating, and ran them through selection loops that varied the judge, the candidate source, and the alternative source. I found that a simple predictive model using first-round measurements gives calibrated endpoint estimates and reproduces the direction, pace, and spread of the real trajectories.

caption: Six candidates per prompt, two kept, train, then re-measure on held-out prompts
narration: For each prompt in a round, the organism writes six candidate answers (the pool) and the judge compares each of them against an alternative. The two most chosen (averaged over orderings) by the judge become that round's training data, and held-out prompts measure the value after each round of training.

caption: Qwen3-4B and OLMo-3-7B, with example answers and their 0-1 value scores
narration: Each organism's value is the mean value score of its answers. For the gambling organism, that is the share that pick the risky gamble. For the insecure-code organism, it is how insecure its answers to three fixed questions about its own coding habits are, scored zero to one by its frozen base model.

caption: Spread times agreement reconstructs the gaps: R² 0.80, MAE 0.040, 367 rounds
narration: Two quantities are measured each round, spread and agreement, and together they forecast the selector gap, the difference between the kept candidates and the whole pool. Spread is the standard deviation of the answers' value scores and agreement is the correlation of the judge's preferences with those scores, both measured within each prompt's pool and averaged over the round's prompts.

caption: One-round rule, held out by condition: MAE 0.081 against 0.128 for no change
narration: The model forecasts the selector gap as candidate spread times judge agreement, so the predicted kept mean is the pool mean plus that product, and training then moves the value to that kept mean. Across every round with logged judge scores, that product reconstructs the realized gaps closely.

caption: Predicted kept mean: MAE 0.100, against 0.085 using the observed kept mean
narration: For endpoints, the model repeats this update from the round-one candidate mean, holding spread, agreement, and pool composition fixed and clipping each step to the zero-to-one scale. Iterated that way, from first-round measurements alone, it predicts a run's final value with a mean absolute error of zero point one one eight on the zero-to-one value scale, against zero point four three one for assuming no change.

caption: 32 self-only four-round runs: endpoint MAE 0.159 against 0.269; horizon 0.100 to 0.130 against 0.31 to 0.43
narration: The background is the change the model predicts for a run starting at each first-round spread and agreement; every dot is a real run, placed by the same two measurements. The dots sit where the background says they should, and they keep sitting there as the forecast reaches further ahead, because a run moves mostly in its first rounds and then levels off.

caption: Where the noise enters, and how each term was sized from the measured residuals
narration: The deterministic forecast only gives the average path that real runs scatter around. The value is read from a limited number of sampled answers, so each reading carries sampling noise, and the loop itself varies: the judge's picks land around spread times agreement rather than exactly on it, training lands near but not exactly on the kept mean, and agreement drifts between rounds. The stochastic version of the model adds a random term at each of these points, with sizes taken from the measured residuals.

caption: Simulated against observed: total change 0.709/0.648, direction changes 1.22/1.20, endpoint SD 0.387/0.370
narration: Sampled forward, the stochastic model reproduces the dynamics of the observed trajectories: the total round-to-round value change over a run is about the same as observed, runs change direction about as often, and eighty-nine percent of final values fall inside the predicted eighty percent band.

caption: Two interventions, aimed at spread and agreement; the oracle judge sets agreement to −1
narration: Both interventions worked through spread and agreement: adding base-model answers to a collapsed pool restored spread, and the judge's agreement then eroded a value that had been stuck, while swapping the base-model judge for a min-risk oracle, which drives agreement to its negative extreme, reversed a run that had climbed near the top of the scale. Each of these is one experiment on one run.

checks: more families, larger models, longer runs; DPO, online RL, constitutional feedback
moral judgment, AI identity, emergent misalignment, internal representations
models revise prompts and edit the loop; repeated games, agentic environments
closer: The forecast is untested outside these two behaviors and these two model families.
narration: The training setup here is narrow: small models, short runs, filtered supervised fine-tuning, a handful of model families, and the risk-preference and insecure-code behaviors. Extensions should scale that up and compare this fine-tuning update with D P O, online reinforcement learning against a learned reward model, and constitutional feedback. The behaviors should widen to moral judgment, A I identity, and emergent misalignment, with readouts that reach past answers into internal representations. More open-ended setups would give models more freedom in selecting training data, revising system prompts, and editing the loop itself. Repeated games and agentic environments could reveal whether the dynamics favor cooperation or defection, resource grabbing, and reward hacking. Natural and cultural selection sculpted human values; value dynamics research can help identify artificial selection mechanisms that can be engineered into virtuous cycles for aligning increasingly autonomous A I systems.
